topic: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
expected_points: MCP is an open standard for connecting AI applications to external tools and data
It defines a client/server architecture over transports such as stdio
It was introduced by Anthropic

topic: How does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) work?
expected_points: A retriever fetches relevant documents from a vector store
Retrieved context is injected into the prompt before generation
It reduces hallucination by grounding answers in source documents

topic: What is LangGraph and how does it differ from LangChain?
expected_points: LangGraph models agent workflows as a stateful graph of nodes and edges
It supports cycles, checkpointing and human-in-the-loop interrupts
LangChain focuses on composing chains rather than durable stateful graphs

topic: Why did DRAM prices rise sharply in 2026?
expected_points: AI and data centre demand pulled manufacturing capacity away from consumer memory
Supply chain constraints and tariffs raised component costs
Consumer RAM became scarce, pushing prices up sharply

topic: What are vector databases used for?
expected_points: They store embeddings and support approximate nearest-neighbour search
They power semantic search and RAG pipelines
Examples include pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate and Qdrant

topic: What is quantization in large language models?
expected_points: Weights are stored at lower numeric precision such as int8 or int4
It reduces memory footprint and speeds up inference
It trades some accuracy for efficiency

topic: How does Ollama run large language models locally?
expected_points: It serves models locally over an HTTP API, by default on port 11434
Models are pulled and stored on the local machine
Inference runs on local hardware, so no data leaves the machine

topic: What is OAuth 2.0 and how does the authorization code flow work?
expected_points: The client redirects the user to an authorization server to obtain consent
An authorization code is exchanged for an access token
Refresh tokens allow new access tokens without re-prompting the user

topic: What are the trade-offs of multi-agent versus single-agent LLM systems?
expected_points: Multi-agent systems allow specialisation and separation of concerns
They add orchestration complexity, latency and cost
Single agents are simpler but harder to control for long workflows

topic: How does PostgreSQL implement MVCC?
expected_points: Each row version carries transaction visibility metadata
Readers do not block writers and writers do not block readers
Dead tuples are reclaimed by VACUUM

topic: What is LLM-as-a-judge evaluation?
expected_points: A language model scores outputs against a rubric instead of exact matching
It suits open-ended generation where string comparison fails
Judge bias and inconsistency are known limitations

topic: What does a checkpointer do in a stateful agent workflow?
expected_points: It persists graph state after each step so a run can be resumed
It enables pausing for human review and later continuation
State is keyed by a thread identifier

topic: What is the difference between fine-tuning and prompt engineering?
expected_points: Fine-tuning updates model weights on task-specific data
Prompt engineering changes only the input, leaving weights untouched
Fine-tuning costs more but can encode behaviour prompts cannot

topic: How do WebSockets differ from HTTP long polling?
expected_points: WebSockets keep a single full-duplex connection open after an upgrade handshake
Long polling repeatedly opens requests that the server holds until data is ready
WebSockets have lower latency and overhead for frequent updates
